title: First-Line Supervisors of Non-Retail Sales Workers

tasks.short: Hear customer complaints, agree a fair remedy, and coordinate resolution.

steps.what: Listen to the customer's complaint and clarify the desired outcome.
Retrieve account history in the {CRM} and order facts from the {ERP}.
Check contractual obligations, complaint guidance, and remedy limits in the {DOCS}.
Choose a proposed remedy or escalate beyond delegated authority.
Discuss the proposed remedy with the customer and agree the next action.
Write and send the remedy confirmation through the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Structured agreed remedy, verified facts, and approved confirmation template
loop.check: Check amounts, dates, and commitments against approved fields; supervisor approves wording and sending.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass, maximum 600 words; use the template manually if checks fail.
loop.why_not_simpler: Complex complaints need individual explanations; standard cases use template filling without a model.

steps.what: Request the approved operational remedy through the {HELPDESK}.
Check completion and close the complaint in the {HELPDESK}.

tasks.design: Join complaint records in the {HELPDESK} to verified account and order facts from the {CRM} and {ERP}, with indexed guidance from the {DOCS}. The supervisor hears the customer and approves the remedy; a template generator uses a bounded drafting loop only for complex confirmations. The {WORKFLOW} routes the approved remedy and returns completion evidence for closure.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaint facts were spread across account records, orders, correspondence, and policy documents. The sensitive conversation made whole-task automation unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic joins can prepare the facts and route remedies. Bounded drafting can reduce writing time while preserving approval of customer commitments.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed facts, staff allegations, and promises outside delegated authority need careful investigation. GDPR requires appropriate access and retention; national employment rules may affect personnel complaints. Any later AI use needs assessment under the EU AI Act.
tasks.human_edge: Hear what the customer considers unfair, acknowledge harm, and negotiate a remedy that restores trust.

ambition.what: Complaint recovery check-in for customers after an agreed remedy

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time collecting facts and arranging paperwork, leaving more time for difficult conversations and recovery follow-up. Remedy authority stays within existing delegation.

reach.task: Plan account recovery after a resolved complaint
reach.learn: Relationship history, renewal risks, and promises requiring follow-up

evidence.claim: Account and order retrieval, template generation, and approved-remedy routing can use deterministic technology.
A bounded model can draft a complaint confirmation from approved facts, but wording and commitments need human review.

assumptions: The supervisor receives escalated complaints; routine inquiries are handled elsewhere.
The representative case begins by phone; email and in-person complaints also occur.
A shared complaint queue exists in the {HELPDESK}, although some teams use the {CRM}.
Remedies beyond delegation require approval before they are offered.
Automated routing creates a work order; it does not independently issue refunds or make staff findings.
The high model-needed prior applies mainly to drafting; listening and negotiation stay human.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Complaint volumes, channels, and current case-record location
Whether customer and order identifiers reliably match
Remedy limits and approval roles for exceptional settlements
How completion and customer acceptance are evidenced
Retention rules and consultation requirements for personnel-related complaints
research_questions: What proportion of confirmations can use fixed templates?
Which draft checks reliably detect new or altered commitments?
What completion evidence is sufficient for closure in each complaint category?
new_work: Review confirmation drafts and approve sending
Investigate unmatched or disputed account facts
Maintain remedy templates, limits, and routing rules
Handle failed operational handoffs
Schedule and conduct complaint recovery check-ins
tasks.statement: Listen to and resolve customer complaints regarding services, products, or personnel.

tasks.short: Review sales results, discuss gaps with staff, and agree corrective actions.

steps.what: Review sales results, pipeline movements, and activity records in the {CRM}.
Reconcile the {CRM} export with booked sales and targets in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Assess gaps against targets, territory conditions, deal timing, and staff experience.
Discuss performance barriers and agree practical support with the sales representative.
Record agreed actions, owners, and review dates in the {CRM}.
Send reminders through the {EMAIL} and request progress updates.

tasks.design: Configure a performance view in the {CRM}; add a scheduled {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciliation with the {ERP} where booked sales differ. A structured action form in the {CRM} records supervisor-approved support and schedules reminders through the {WORKFLOW}. The supervisor interprets gaps and conducts the conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Targets, deal ownership, and booked revenue often used different definitions. Weekly exports compensated for those differences.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting can cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can shorten connector and validation development once definitions are agreed.
tasks.still_hard: Territory quality and delayed bookings complicate fair comparisons. GDPR applies to staff records; national consultation rules may apply to monitoring schemes. Adding AI performance evaluation would require an EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish weak selling from weak territory conditions, build trust, and choose support that fits the person.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of deals needing supervisor support

tasks.altitude: The week contains less report assembly and more focused coaching and deal support. The supervisor can select support priorities within existing authority; pay and disciplinary rights do not expand.

reach.task: Review pipeline coverage for the next forecast
reach.learn: Revenue definitions, forecast categories, and territory comparability

evidence.claim: Scheduled sales reports, reconciliation rules, and dashboards can use structured records without a model.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales supports sales-data questions and open-deal risk flags; this does not validate employee ratings.
The cited sales-agent experiments found benefits from combining AI feedback with a human manager.
Dutch works council consent provisions include staff-data and performance-monitoring schemes; other national rules vary.
AI used to monitor or evaluate worker performance is listed in the EU AI Act employment high-risk category.

assumptions: A typical team uses the {CRM}, with a workbook bridging booked revenue and targets.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Preparation occupies more time than the prior suggests when revenue reconciliation is manual.
The design uses arithmetic and supervisor judgement, without model-generated employee scores.
Consultation and access ranges allow for staff-monitoring review; elapsed time may be longer.
unknowns: Whether the {CRM} already reports booked revenue accurately
Target definitions, ownership rules, and territory changes
Applicable national consultation procedures and existing approvals
The supervisor's authority over coaching, targets, and formal personnel actions
research_questions: Which native reporting features cover the required comparisons?
Which reconciliation checks best reveal booking and ownership errors?
How should small samples and territory differences be displayed fairly?
new_work: Review unmatched revenue and ownership exceptions
Maintain target definitions and connector mappings
Check dashboard access and retention settings
Confirm action records accurately reflect the conversation
tasks.statement: Monitor sales staff performance to ensure that goals are met.

tasks.short: Hire sales staff, arrange their training, coach them and evaluate their performance.

steps.what: Define the staffing need and prepare a role brief.
Review applications and propose candidates for interview.
Interview candidates and assess relevant sales skills.
Choose the candidate and approve the proposed offer terms.
Prepare the offer package, check it and send it for signature.
Select training modules and set onboarding milestones.
Demonstrate sales techniques, practise customer conversations and give coaching feedback.
Check course completions and follow up missing training.
Compile sales results, agreed goals and previous feedback for evaluation.
Discuss performance, hear the employee's explanation and agree an evaluation.
Write and approve the evaluation record and development actions.

loop.input: The supervisor's evaluation decision, development actions and selected supporting evidence.
loop.output: A draft evaluation record that expresses the supervisor's assessment.
loop.check: Trace statements to supplied notes; forbid inferred ratings or traits; supervisor checks meaning and fairness.
loop.stop: One draft and one requested revision; otherwise the supervisor writes the record.
loop.why_not_simpler: Individual explanations need free-text wording; fixed fields alone cannot express them clearly.

tasks.design: Configure role templates, offer packages and onboarding flows across the {ATS}, {HCM}, {ESIGN} and {LMS}. A deterministic evidence pack combines agreed metrics from the {CRM} and {TALENT}; a bounded loop drafts the supervisor's evaluation record, with approval before storage or employee release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hiring, learning and performance records sit in separate systems. Much of the work also depends on trust, observation and individual circumstances.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates and workflow configuration can remove repeated administration. Small integrations can assemble evidence without introducing automated candidate ranking or performance scoring.
tasks.still_hard: Hiring judgement, effective coaching and fair evaluation remain demanding. GDPR, national employment rules and consultation can make employee-data changes slower than coding.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor hears context, notices confidence and skill gaps, and gives feedback the employee can act on.

ambition.what: A first-month sales practice clinic for new starters.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor uses saved preparation time for observed practice and individual development. Hiring, pay and promotion authority remain within existing delegations.

reach.task: Practise discovery questions and follow-up for a stalled opportunity.
reach.learn: The representative's sales cycle, customer objections and evidence of useful coaching.

reach.task: Teach new starters when to request technical qualification support.
reach.learn: Technical discovery boundaries and the information needed for a useful handoff.

evidence.claim: Configured hiring, training and evaluation workflows can reduce administrative work while people make employment decisions.
Sales-agent experiments found differing responses to AI coaching and better results when managers relayed AI feedback.
Employment-related AI evaluation can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk categories; applicability needs assessment.
GDPR Article 22 concerns solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

assumptions: The sales supervisor contributes to hiring; a recruiter and hiring manager hold their stated responsibilities.
Steps include collaborator time so handoffs are visible; shares describe the combined task rather than one individual's timesheet.
Conversations and judgement dominate, consistent with the human-work prior.
The draft evaluation restates a human assessment and does not infer employee ratings.
Build ranges estimate one team's pilot; consultation and access are working effort, and elapsed approval time may be longer.
Employee-data use follows GDPR; consultation follows national rules, including Dutch works council requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Who may shortlist candidates, approve offers and submit evaluations?
Which hiring, learning and performance systems are available?
Which metrics employees have been told are used for evaluation?
What consultation or consent requirements apply under national rules?
Whether drafting assistance is acceptable to employees and their representatives.
research_questions: Can existing templates cover evaluation wording well enough to avoid a model loop?
What is the current legal classification of drafting a human assessment without scoring employees?
How should evidence packs display territory differences and missing data without implying a ranking?
new_work: Check offer packages before sending.
Review training plans and handle unsuitable module assignments.
Correct incomplete or misleading evaluation evidence.
Review drafted evaluation wording.
Maintain templates, access permissions and retention settings.

tasks.short: Develop sales methods, market expansion plans and promotional approaches with senior colleagues.

steps.what: Gather sales, pipeline and campaign results for the planning discussion.
Prepare possible sales methods and market experiments for discussion.

loop.input: Commercial evidence, customer feedback and the current sales playbook.
loop.output: An options brief with hypotheses, supporting evidence, uncertainties and proposed tests.
loop.check: Trace factual claims to inputs; calculate figures deterministically; supervisor checks commercial plausibility.
loop.stop: One brief with at most three options and one revision; missing evidence stays explicit.
loop.why_not_simpler: Options require synthesising free-text feedback and writing testable hypotheses; metrics use deterministic code.

steps.what: Discuss options with sales, marketing and finance leaders.
Approve the pilot scope, budget and success criteria.
Write the agreed procedure and pilot plan.

loop.input: Approved pilot scope, budget, success criteria and current procedure.
loop.output: A pilot plan and proposed procedure changes with decision references.
loop.check: Match every commitment to the approved decision; flag missing owners, dates or instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; ambiguous commitments return to the supervisor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each pilot changes free-text working instructions; a template supplies structure but not all wording.

steps.what: Publish agreed instructions and allocate pilot actions to colleagues.

tasks.design: A reusable evidence dashboard joins approved data from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, while a bounded loop drafts an options brief in the {DOCS}. People choose and approve the pilot; configured flows in the {PROJECT} publish checked instructions, assign actions and collect results for the next discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence takes time to assemble, while commercial choices are too contextual for fixed rules. Meeting decisions often remain buried in notes and email.
tasks.enabler_now: Small data joins and standard experiment templates are easier to build. Bounded drafting can turn supplied evidence and decisions into usable briefs.
tasks.still_hard: Market uncertainty, competing priorities and weak attribution remain. A persuasive draft can still describe an unworkable idea.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor knows which methods sellers can execute and can negotiate trade-offs with other leaders.

ambition.what: A weekly stop, extend or redesign decision for one customer-segment pilot.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor arrives with evidence and testable options, then follows pilot outcomes more frequently. Budget and market-entry approval remain with the sales manager unless explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Decide whether to extend a customer-segment pilot.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, experimental uncertainty and delegated budget limits.

reach.task: Test a revised commercial proposition with prospective customers.
reach.learn: How to record objections and distinguish interest from a credible buying signal.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales supports questions on sales data and open-deal risk signals.
The cited sales-data capability supports evidence preparation; it does not establish autonomous commercial strategy.
Deterministic metric packs and configured pilot tracking can support human strategy discussions.

assumptions: Sales methods and market expansion are agreed with senior colleagues rather than decided by the supervisor alone.
Discussion and approval consume most time, consistent with the human-work prior.
The evidence pack uses existing approved data and avoids collecting new customer data by default.
Build ranges estimate one team, a small metric set and one pilot template.
Access review includes GDPR and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Which commercial metrics and cost data are accessible?
Who approves budgets, procedures and market-entry decisions?
Whether customer feedback can be used in an approved model environment.
What pilot volume permits meaningful measurement?
Which data-residency and retention requirements apply?
research_questions: Which existing dashboard configuration can produce the evidence pack without custom joins?
What comparison design can distinguish pilot effects from seasonality and account mix?
Can structured decision forms remove the need for the procedure-drafting loop?
new_work: Check draft hypotheses and their supporting evidence.
Maintain metric definitions and pilot templates.
Check published procedures against approved decisions.
Collect pilot outcomes and document inconclusive results.
Monitor model access, retention and data processing location.
tasks.statement: Confer with company officials to develop methods and procedures to increase sales, expand markets, and promote business.

tasks.short: Help sales staff handle difficult deals, technical questions, and unusual customer requirements.

steps.what: Hear the sales representative's problem and clarify the customer requirement.
Find approved guidance and relevant product information in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Clarified assistance request and permission-filtered approved guidance
loop.output: Short guidance pack with source passages and unresolved questions
loop.check: Verify document access, current versions, and citations; supervisor checks applicability.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one answer pass, at most eight passages; abstain when unsupported.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests use varied language and need several passages combined; exact search remains the fallback.

steps.what: Choose an approach and identify issues needing specialist approval.
Work through the difficult duty with the sales representative and practise the approach.
Record agreed next steps and escalation owners in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Use existing search in the {DOCS} first, adding a bounded answer loop where questions require combining approved passages. The supervisor checks the guidance and coaches the representative; a configured form in the {CRM} captures actions and routes specialist escalations through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful guidance was scattered, inconsistently named, and difficult to connect to a specific customer situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Permission-aware retrieval and small source-grounded reading loops can prepare a useful guidance pack. The coaching conversation needs no technical breakthrough.
tasks.still_hard: Missing or outdated guidance still requires an expert. Technical commitments and contract exceptions need the relevant approver. GDPR applies to customer and staff information; an extension into AI employee evaluation needs separate EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Understand where the representative is stuck, demonstrate judgement, and build confidence without overwhelming them.

ambition.what: Weekly difficult-deal clinic for junior sales representatives

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time searching and can reserve a regular slot for difficult-deal coaching. They gain no new authority to approve technical claims or contract exceptions.

reach.task: Qualify technical requirements before preparing a solution
reach.learn: Technical discovery questions, product limits, and escalation criteria

evidence.claim: Approved-document retrieval can support a bounded, cited guidance draft, with human checks for applicability.
Sales-agent coaching experiments found different responses by ability level and benefits from manager-relayed AI feedback.

assumptions: Most assistance involves judgement and conversation rather than paperwork, consistent with the prior.
Approved guidance exists in the {DOCS} and has identifiable owners.
Representatives provide a short request; routine conversation recording is unnecessary.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
The guidance loop supports deal work and does not rate staff.
unknowns: Coverage and freshness of approved sales guidance
Access restrictions across customer and product documents
Which requests require specialist approval
Whether staff consultation is required for the proposed use
research_questions: Does existing document search already answer common assistance requests?
How often does retrieval return outdated or conflicting guidance?
What answer length helps inexperienced representatives without creating overload?
new_work: Review source-grounded guidance before using it
Escalate unsupported questions to specialists
Maintain document ownership and expiry rules
Test retrieval permissions and abstention behaviour
tasks.statement: Provide staff with assistance in performing difficult or complicated duties.

tasks.short: Prepare sales-team schedules, assign duties and adjust coverage when availability or customer demand changes.

steps.what: Check contracted hours, leave and recorded absences.
Collect availability changes and scheduling preferences from employees.
Estimate coverage needs from customer appointments, open orders and planned campaigns.
Build a draft roster that fits coverage, hours and available skills.
Discuss duty assignments and resolve coverage conflicts with employees.
Check working-time limits, coverage and fairness before approving the schedule.
Publish the approved schedule and notify employees of their duties.
Resolve later absence or swap requests and approve schedule changes.

tasks.design: Configure workforce scheduling in the {OTHER}, using approved availability from the {HCM} and deterministic coverage estimates from the {CRM} and {ERP}. Hard constraints check hours, rest and agreed qualifications; the supervisor resolves duty conflicts and approves schedules and changes before configured notifications publish them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coverage needs, absences and employee preferences arrive through different channels. A workbook is flexible, but checking constraints and distributing changes takes repeated effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workforce scheduling software already supports availability, constraints and swaps. Small mappings can adapt it to non-retail sales coverage without a model or autonomous agent.
tasks.still_hard: Customer continuity, scarce skills and competing preferences require judgement. National working-time rules, collective agreements and consultation can constrain configuration.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor recognises hidden workload, negotiates fair compromises and protects important customer relationships.

ambition.what: A daily customer-coverage recovery decision when absence leaves a gap.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time assembling rosters and more time balancing customer coverage and employee needs. Schedule approval stays with the supervisor; contractual changes remain outside that authority.

reach.task: Plan callback coverage around promised customer contact times.
reach.learn: Contact windows, queue demand and the skills needed for each call type.

reach.task: Reserve technical support capacity for qualified customer appointments.
reach.learn: Qualification requirements, preparation time and the cost of interrupting technical work.

evidence.claim: Quinyx supports demand-based schedules, working-time constraints and employee swaps.
Kendra Scott's vendor case reports faster scheduling and personnel-budget savings; transfer to non-retail sales is unproven.
Dutch works council consent can apply to working-time schemes, staff-data arrangements and performance-monitoring tools.
AI allocation based on individual behaviour or traits can fall within the EU AI Act's employment high-risk category.

assumptions: The team needs shared customer coverage; many employees otherwise have stable contracted hours.
A {SPREADSHEET} currently bridges the roster, availability messages and system data.
Structured scheduling consumes more time than the meeting-heavy prior suggests; duty negotiation remains human.
The {OTHER} is a workforce scheduling system with suitable constraint and approval features.
Availability forms collect scheduling information without requesting medical explanations.
Build ranges estimate one team's configuration and include employee consultation, access and national-rule review.
Configured deterministic scheduling uses agreed qualifications and availability, without model-based employee scoring.
unknowns: Does the company already have workforce scheduling capability?
Which national working-time rules and collective agreements apply?
What consultation or works council consent is required?
Which customer commitments and skills create hard coverage constraints?
How frequently do absences or swaps disrupt coverage?
Can employees submit availability through a structured form?
research_questions: Can existing scheduling configuration represent customer continuity and technical-support coverage?
Which deterministic coverage estimate is accurate enough for this sales team's workload?
What current EU AI Act requirements apply if later changes introduce AI-based employee allocation?
new_work: Review draft rosters and uncovered demand.
Resolve preference conflicts and exceptional duty assignments.
Maintain working-time constraints and qualification records.
Approve schedule changes and monitor failed notifications.
Review fairness concerns with employees and their representatives.
tasks.statement: Plan and prepare work schedules, and assign employees to specific duties.

tasks.short: Exchange product information and agree cross-department sales actions in company meetings.

steps.what: Read product updates and open actions before the meeting.
Exchange agenda items and confirm participants.
Discuss product changes, customer questions and technical constraints.
Agree priorities, owners and dates for cross-department actions.
Write the meeting record and action list.

loop.input: Written product clarifications and coordination decisions captured by participants.
loop.output: Draft meeting record and action list with source references.
loop.check: Check every owner, date and commitment against the notes. The supervisor approves publication.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt per meeting. Missing facts remain blank; failure returns to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes vary. Templates can format them but cannot reliably condense their meaning.

steps.what: Send action reminders and ask owners for progress.

tasks.design: A deterministic briefing generator links current product updates in {DOCS} to open actions in {PROJECT}; {CALENDAR} collects agenda items. A bounded loop drafts records from written notes for supervisor approval, then {WORKFLOW} creates approved actions and reminders in {PROJECT}. People retain the discussion and agreement of cross-department commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Updates and actions sit in separate places. Small preparation savings rarely justified bespoke integration.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and reminder features handle routine coordination. AI-assisted coding can reduce the cost of connecting records and building a briefing template.
tasks.still_hard: Departments must resolve competing priorities themselves. Access controls, GDPR retention and any consultation under national rules still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an unstated constraint and negotiating a commitment another department can actually keep.

ambition.what: A twice-weekly decision on unresolved product blockers affecting live sales opportunities.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less agenda assembly and chasing, but discussion still dominates. No decision rights change automatically; the supervisor can seek delegated authority to convene urgent product-blocker decisions.

reach.task: Prepare technical answers for unresolved customer questions.
reach.learn: Product limits, technical dependencies and when specialist validation is required.

reach.task: Prioritise cross-department blockers across sales teams.
reach.learn: Commercial impact, escalation thresholds and capacity trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Agenda collection, action reminders and structured briefings can use configured workflows and deterministic code.
A bounded model loop can draft minutes from written notes; commitments still require source checks.

assumptions: These are recurring internal coordination meetings, not formal consultation proceedings.
Discussion and agreement occupy 80% of current time, close to the meeting-heavy prior.
Participants supply written notes; recording or transcription is not assumed.
Build ranges are estimates for one team using existing systems. Approval waiting time may extend the calendar duration.
unknowns: Where product updates and action lists are currently maintained.
Whether departments already use shared agenda and action features.
Who can approve commitments for each department.
Which employee consultation, access and retention arrangements apply.
research_questions: Can existing agenda and action features remove the need for custom integration?
How reliably can short meeting notes support source-linked drafts without recording conversations?
new_work: Check drafted commitments, owners and dates.
Resolve unmatched actions and outdated product links.
Maintain agenda templates, access groups and reminder rules.
tasks.statement: Attend company meetings to exchange product information and coordinate work activities with other departments.

tasks.short: Prepare sales and inventory reports for management and budget planning.

steps.what: Export sales activity and transaction figures for the reporting period.
Retrieve inventory balances, movements and outstanding orders.
Join exports, standardise periods and calculate report measures.
Resolve differences against finance totals and confirm reporting cut-offs.
Build the sales and inventory tables, charts and report document.
Explain material variances and approve the report for release.
Email report attachments to management and budget recipients.

tasks.design: Scheduled exports from {CRM}, {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed deterministic joins and reconciliation checks on {DATA_PLATFORM}; unresolved differences go to the finance team. Configured {BI} templates generate reports and variance tables, then the supervisor adds explanations and approves release to authorised viewers. Shared access to the approved report replaces emailed attachments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identifiers, reporting cut-offs and measure definitions differed across exports. Manual workbook joins became the practical bridge between systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled exports, report templates and deterministic reconciliation already exist. AI-assisted coding can reduce the cost of the remaining connectors and checks.
tasks.still_hard: Late postings, returns and stock timing can create real differences. Reliable reports still require agreed definitions, clear exception ownership and appropriate GDPR access controls.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a data problem from a commercial problem and explaining what management should do next.

ambition.what: A daily review of stock-related sales risks before the next customer commitments.

tasks.altitude: Routine report assembly largely disappears, leaving variance investigation and management explanation. With delegation, the supervisor can prioritise stock-risk follow-up; purchasing and budget authority do not change automatically.

reach.task: Turn material sales variances into a revised team forecast.
reach.learn: Forecast assumptions, variance attribution and management reporting.

reach.task: Investigate stock-related order exceptions before confirming delivery.
reach.learn: Inventory status, order cut-offs and fulfilment escalation.

evidence.claim: Scheduled joins, reconciliation checks and report templates can automate structured sales and inventory reporting without a model.
Dynamics 365 Sales supports questions on sales data; this does not establish inventory reconciliation or report accuracy.
GDPR Article 22 concerns qualifying solely automated decisions about individuals, rather than every automated report.

assumptions: Reporting combines structured sales and inventory data, with a workbook bridging systems today.
The report supports management decisions rather than automatically determining employee pay or performance ratings.
Recipients accept a shared approved report instead of emailed attachments.
Configured report generation also produces the variance table used during review.
The supervisor's commentary remains manual; prefilled figures reduce its preparation time.
Build ranges are estimates for one reporting scope. They include parallel report comparison during rollout.
unknowns: Current reporting tools, manual joins and recipient requirements.
Availability of scheduled exports or supported interfaces.
Definitions of sales, returns, stock availability and reporting cut-offs.
Who owns reconciliation exceptions and report release.
Whether reports contain individual employee performance measures.
Applicable employee consultation and access requirements under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing reporting features eliminate the workbook bridge?
Which control totals and cut-off tests reliably catch material discrepancies?
If employee-level evaluation is introduced, which GDPR and EU AI Act obligations apply?
new_work: Review reconciliation exceptions and failed data refreshes.
Maintain measure definitions, mappings and report access.
Explain material variances and approve report release.
Check source totals after changes to finance or inventory processes.
tasks.statement: Prepare sales and inventory reports for management and budget departments.

tasks.short: Set merchandise pricing policies that meet profitability requirements and commercial goals.

steps.what: Collect current costs, realised prices, discounts and sales volumes.
Check cost allocation, rebates and unusual margin differences.
Calculate margin scenarios for price bands and discount limits.
Choose price bands, discount limits and exception criteria.
Approve the pricing policy and its commercial limits.
Publish the approved policy and update operational pricing rules.

tasks.design: Deterministic jobs join costs and realised prices from {ERP} and {CRM}, validate agreed cost rules, and expose margin scenarios in {BI}. The supervisor chooses policy and the sales manager approves it; configured {WORKFLOW} then publishes the approved version in {DOCS} and applies supported pricing rules in {CRM} and {ERP}. No model loop is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost definitions and discount data differed across systems. Policy choices also required commercial judgement, making whole-task automation unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: Scenario arithmetic and validation rules are straightforward to encode. AI-assisted coding can make a small, auditable pricing workbench cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Rebates, freight, customer agreements and competitor reactions can change the apparent margin. Cost definitions and legal scope must be settled before rules are applied.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing margin against retention, positioning and promises already made to customers.

ambition.what: A weekly margin-band review for product groups with recent cost changes.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends more time comparing commercial trade-offs and less time calculating scenarios. If authority is delegated, the supervisor can approve discounts within an agreed margin band; wider policy remains with the sales manager.

reach.task: Set discount delegation limits across teams.
reach.learn: Portfolio margin, customer retention economics and commercial governance.

reach.task: Prepare a quote within approved price and discount bands.
reach.learn: Quote economics, contractual exceptions and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Margin calculations, discount limits and price ladders can use deterministic rules; selecting policy remains judgement.
Where EU consumer price-announcement rules apply, stated reductions use the relevant prior-price reference.

assumptions: The company sells merchandise through non-retail sales teams.
Policy changes are considered when costs or market conditions change; routine review need not change policy.
The sales manager holds final policy authority.
The existing systems support approved pricing rules; otherwise publication needs a deterministic connector.
The scenario tool uses explicit assumptions rather than claiming to predict demand response.
Build ranges are estimates for a limited product and currency scope.
unknowns: The agreed profitability measure and treatment of freight, rebates and returns.
Which contracts override standard pricing.
Whether sales are business-to-business, consumer-facing or mixed.
Which systems enforce prices and discount limits.
Current approval rights and possible delegated discount authority.
Whether employee consultation under national rules applies to the proposed change.
research_questions: Which existing pricing features can enforce versioned rules without custom code?
Which consumer price-announcement requirements apply to the relevant channels and merchandise?
Can actual transaction margins be reconciled accurately enough for policy decisions?
new_work: Resolve cost and contract exceptions.
Maintain margin definitions and scenario assumptions.
Review proposed policy changes and delegated limits.
Check published rule versions and monitor realised margins.
tasks.statement: Formulate pricing policies on merchandise according to profitability requirements.

tasks.short: Check product prices, presentation and advertised functions, then arrange corrections.

steps.what: Retrieve approved prices, display instructions and advertised product claims.
Compare displayed prices and presentation with the approved references.
Test demonstrated functions against the advertised product claims.
Decide which discrepancies require correction, withdrawal or specialist investigation.
Correct physical labels and displays, or remove unsuitable demonstration products.
Publish approved price corrections to the customer-facing catalogue.
Record completed corrections and notify the owner of unresolved issues.

tasks.design: A deterministic job combines approved prices from the {ERP} with versioned display instructions and claims from {DOCS}. A mobile form in {WORKFLOW} supports physical checks, prepares replacement labels and routes unresolved findings. Approved catalogue price corrections pass through a validated connector to {ECOMMERCE}, with approval attached to publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical presentation and functional checks depend on context. Price references, product claims and correction records often sit apart.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured product identifiers, versioned references and simple forms can connect the administrative work. Deterministic comparisons handle prices where both values are available as data.

tasks.short: Assess territory growth potential and propose fair, achievable sales quotas.

steps.what: Export territory sales, pipeline and account coverage data.
Reconcile territory mappings, periods, currencies and missing account data.
Assess growth, penetration, pipeline quality and account concentration by territory.
Calculate quota scenarios against revenue targets, capacity and territory potential.
Recommend quotas and explain territory-specific adjustments.
Challenge assumptions and approve or revise the quota proposal.
Enter approved quotas and distribute the territory plan.

tasks.design: Scheduled connectors reconcile {CRM} and {ERP} data in the {DATA_PLATFORM} and feed a territory dashboard in {BI}. Deterministic scenario calculations expose assumptions, capacity limits and target totals; the supervisor adds commercial judgement. A recorded sales manager approval releases quota updates to the {CRM} through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Territory mappings and definitions differ between sales and finance. Quota politics and uncertain market potential cannot be settled by a calculation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing data connectors, dashboards and versioned calculation rules make repeatable scenarios practical. AI-assisted coding can shorten development, but data definitions still need agreement.
tasks.still_hard: Market potential is only partly observable. Inherited account quality, vacancies, long sales cycles and quota-linked pay can make apparently equal targets unfair.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing commercial context, explaining trade-offs and negotiating targets that people can defend.

ambition.what: Hold a monthly territory-capacity review between formal quota-setting rounds.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor shifts from assembling quarterly workbooks to investigating territory constraints and preparing monthly capacity options. They gain faster scenario access; the sales manager retains quota approval.

reach.task: Allocate sales capacity across territories.
reach.learn: Interpret scenario sensitivity, distinguish potential from pipeline, and assess quota effects on incentives.

reach.task: Prioritise under-covered accounts within a territory.
reach.learn: Use account coverage and potential measures without treating uncertain estimates as facts.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales supports sales-data questions and open-deal risk flags; this does not establish automated quota-setting capability.
Territory reconciliation, quota arithmetic and scenario comparisons can use deterministic code.
GDPR Article 22 concerns solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; quota decisions require assessment of their actual effects.
If AI is added to employee task allocation or performance evaluation, its intended use must be assessed against the EU AI Act employment provisions.

assumptions: The supervisor proposes quotas and a sales manager approves them.

Maintain calculation definitions and versioned scenario assumptions.
Review unusual quota changes and document commercial adjustments.
Monitor access permissions and retain approval records.
Compare scenario assumptions with later outcomes.
tasks.statement: Analyze details of sales territories to assess their growth potential and to set quotas.

tasks.short: Visit retailers and sales representatives to explain products, understand needs and agree follow-up.

steps.what: Review account history, open opportunities and previous visit records.
Arrange the visit and confirm the agenda with the contact.
Select approved product material and demonstration examples.
Travel to the retailer or sales representative.
Explain products, observe needs and discuss next steps.
Enter visit findings, needs and commitments into the account record.

loop.input: Supervisor-written visit notes and explicitly agreed commitments.
loop.output: Proposed structured visit record and follow-up plan with source references.
loop.check: Validate account identifiers and field types. Check needs, owners and dates against notes before supervisor approval.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per visit. Unclear fields remain unset; failures use manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Visit notes express needs and commitments in varied language. Fixed fields alone still require manual interpretation.

steps.what: Send agreed material and confirm follow-up commitments.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator assembles account briefings from {CRM}, while configured {CALENDAR} and {DOCS} features prepare appointments and approved visit packs. A bounded extraction loop proposes records and follow-up tasks in {CRM} for approval; {EMAIL} templates prepare external follow-up for a separate send approval. Travel, product discussion and relationship building remain with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account information and approved materials were scattered. Visit findings arrived as informal notes that required manual interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable templates and system connections reduce preparation costs. A small extraction loop can turn written notes into proposed fields without controlling the visit.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, physical observation and credible demonstrations remain personal. GDPR, contact permissions and customer confidentiality constrain note access and retention.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what the contact leaves unsaid, testing product fit and making credible commitments.

ambition.what: A quarterly product clinic for small reseller accounts that currently receive little supervisor attention.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time preparing packs and entering visit records, though travel and conversations still dominate. Existing commercial authority remains; serving smaller accounts requires agreement on visit priorities.

reach.task: Qualify a newly discovered account need and arrange the next conversation.
reach.learn: Discovery questions, buying roles and qualification criteria.

reach.task: Design a demonstration around the customer's operating constraints.
reach.learn: Technical fit, demonstration limits and specialist escalation.

evidence.claim: Structured account briefings and approved-material selection can use deterministic retrieval and templates.
Dynamics 365 Sales supports questions on sales data, demonstrating sales-data assistance rather than autonomous customer visits.
Source-checked extraction can reduce note entry while leaving commercial commitments with the supervisor.

Check extracted needs, commitments and dates.

tasks.short: Maintain purchase, sales and requisition records, reconcile discrepancies and obtain approval for corrections.

steps.what: Retrieve purchase, sales and requisition records from operational systems.
Read emailed purchase confirmations and supporting documents for missing transaction details.

loop.input: Purchase confirmations with missing fields identified from source transaction records.
loop.output: Typed transaction fields with source passages and unresolved fields.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, dates, currency and totals; show source passages for uncertain fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unresolved fields return to the supervisor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Some confirmations contain free text and changing layouts; structured records bypass the loop.

steps.what: Enter missing details and attach supporting documents to transaction records.
Copy transaction details into a local tracking workbook.
Compare recorded transactions against source orders and identify mismatches.
Ask order clerks or the finance team to explain mismatches and propose corrections.
Approve financially material corrections and release them for entry.

A bounded extractor reads irregular confirmations from the {DOCS}; validated fields update records, while financially material corrections require finance approval and duplicate tracking in the {SPREADSHEET} ends.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identifiers and document formats differ across systems. A local workbook often bridges gaps that existing configuration never resolved.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing import features handle standard records. Faster development makes field mappings, validation rules and a small document extractor affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Missing order references, credit notes and disputed ownership still require investigation. Financial posting permissions need careful separation from record maintenance.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor understands why a transaction looks unusual and can get the right colleague to resolve it.

ambition.what: A daily unresolved-order exception service for order clerks.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time copying records and more time resolving recurring order failures. Financial approval rights stay with the finance team.

reach.task: Resolve sales orders blocked by missing purchase references.
reach.learn: Order identifiers, credit-note handling and the boundary between order corrections and ledger postings.

evidence.claim: Scheduled transaction imports, validation and exception reports can use deterministic technology.

tasks.short: Coordinate promotions, prepare sales materials and displays, and approve campaign delivery.

steps.what: Agree the promotion objective, audience and constraints with the sales and marketing teams.
Check account segments and recent sales activity in the {CRM}.
Check stock, prices and margins in the {ERP}.
Agree the offer, responsibilities and delivery dates with the marketing team.
Draft advertising copy and display instructions in {DOCS}.

Approve the final copy, offer terms and display before customer exposure.
Publish the approved promotion page through the {CMS}.
Schedule the approved campaign send in {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
Resolve readiness problems and review early customer responses with the sales team.

A template generator in {WORKFLOW} uses a bounded drafting loop for copy in {DOCS}; approved versions flow to the {CMS} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}. Approval binds the exact content, audience and timing, and any change requires renewed approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Offer facts, copy and delivery responsibilities sit in separate systems. Coordination and physical presentation still need people.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval and scheduling features can handle delivery. AI coding reduces the effort of connecting records and templates; bounded drafting can produce a first version.
tasks.still_hard: Persuasive offers, credible claims and team commitments require judgement. Contact permissions, stock changes and physical displays need reliable checks.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor understands customer objections, resolves competing team priorities and judges whether an offer deserves attention.

ambition.what: Weekly promotion continuation, adjustment or withdrawal decisions using response and margin evidence.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less fact gathering and copy assembly, while coordination remains substantial. Within a delegated budget, the supervisor gains a weekly decision on whether to continue, adjust or stop a promotion.

reach.learn: Learn account segmentation, contact permissions and how to record customer objections.

A bounded drafting loop can prepare copy, but factual checks and publication approval remain necessary.
GDPR applies to contact data; national rules determine any employee consultation required by changed processes.

tasks.short: Prepare rental or lease agreements with agreed charges, payment terms and signatures.

steps.what: Retrieve customer details and the rental request from the {CRM}.
Check equipment availability and identify the item in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Calculate rental charges, deposits and payment dates in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Resolve requested exceptions to standard charges or lease terms.
Populate the agreement template in {DOCS} with equipment, charges and payment procedures.
Check the completed agreement and approve its release to the customer.
Send the approved agreement for signatures through {ESIGN}.
Review and sign the agreement through {ESIGN}.
File the completed agreement and key dates in the {CLM}.
Enter the agreed billing schedule in the {ERP}.

The supervisor approves the exact agreement and recipients before {ESIGN} sends it; completed signatures trigger filing in {CLM} and creation of the billing schedule in the {ERP}. tasks.enabler_now: Template filling, signature workflows and fixed calculations are established capabilities. AI coding makes the remaining connectors and validation rules cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Availability can change before signature. Nonstandard liability, cancellation or payment terms still require commercial and sometimes legal judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor negotiates workable exceptions and recognises terms that create an unacceptable commercial commitment.

reach.learn: Learn deposit treatment, payment dates, equipment identifiers and duplicate prevention.

reach.task: Approve rental terms outside the supervisor's commercial limits.
reach.learn: Learn delegation thresholds, margin implications and liability escalation.

tasks.short: Check stock, resolve discrepancies and reorder products at approved thresholds.

steps.what: Check recorded stock, reservations and incoming deliveries.
Count relevant physical stock and note damaged or unavailable units.
Reconcile count differences and approve stock adjustments.
Compare available stock with reorder levels and calculate required quantities.
Enter replenishment quantities and supplier details into a purchase requisition.
Review quantities, spending limits and exceptions before approving the purchase.
Issue the approved purchase order to the supplier.

tasks.design: Configure stock availability and reorder rules in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, including reservations, incoming orders, pack sizes and supplier lead times. tasks.previous_blocker: Stock accuracy, unreliable lead times and disconnected purchasing records made unattended ordering difficult. Reorder functionality may already exist but be poorly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured inventory and purchasing functions already cover most threshold ordering. Better identifiers and small connectors can remove spreadsheet calculations and requisition re-entry.
tasks.still_hard: Physical stock accuracy, shortages, obsolete goods and supplier constraints remain operational problems. Thresholds need maintenance when demand or lead times change.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparent stock shortage reflects damaged goods, a customer commitment or an unreliable supplier.

tasks.short: Inspect received products and decide whether to accept, quarantine or reject them.

Inspect packaging, product condition and any required sample functions.
Decide whether to accept, quarantine or reject the products.
Record findings and update the stock disposition.
Send discrepancy details to the purchasing and warehouse teams.

tasks.human_edge: Recognising an unusual defect and judging whether it affects safety, saleability or customer expectations.

tasks.short: Coordinate sales staff, allocate duties, resolve blockers, and check operational completion.

steps.what: Review open sales activities and overdue work in the {CRM}.
Discuss availability, urgent customer needs, and blockers in a team huddle.
Allocate duties and deadlines in the {CRM}, considering skills and customer continuity.
Observe work, answer questions, and intervene when delivery or customer commitments are at risk.
Check completion and operational reconciliation exceptions in the {ERP}.
Assign exception owners and request resolution through the {EMAIL}.
